title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: right prayer for others does not require certain faith that our prayers will save them — outcomes are contingent; command to pray for all (even enemies) suffices
pass_a_gloss: Unto prayers rightly to be conceived for other men it is not required that it be persuaded unto us by the certainty of faith that our prayers will be profitable unto them unto salvation. For nothing either false or contingent can underlie our faith; but it is plainly contingent and uncertain whether they will perceive any profit from our prayers. It suffices that God has commanded us to embrace all men with charity, and to pray for others, even for enemies.
pass_b_english: To form prayers rightly for other people, we need not be persuaded by certainty of faith that our prayers will profit them unto salvation. Nothing false or contingent can underlie our faith; yet whether they will gain any profit from our prayers is plainly contingent and uncertain. It is enough that God has commanded us to embrace all men in charity, and to pray for others — even for enemies.
source_text: Ad preces rite concipiendas pro aliis hominibus non requiritur, ut certitudine fidei nobis persuasum sit, preces nostras illis ad salutem profuturas. Nam fidei nostrae nihil aut falsum aut contingens subesse potest; at plane contingens et incertum est, utrum illi aliquid emolumenti ex precibus nostris sint percepturi. Sufficit quod Deus praeceperit nos omnes homines charitate complecti, et pro aliis, etiam pro inimicis, orare.
